title: The text discusses the ongoing political crisis in Kenya, highlighting the challenges to democracy in Africa, particularly the 'sit-tight syndrome' where leaders cling to power. Following disputed elections on December 27, violence erupted between rival tribes, leading to deaths and destruction in slums like Huruma and Mathare. Opposition leader Mr. Odinga claims he was robbed of victory and has called for protests, while the government insists there is no crisis. The Roman Catholic Church and former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan have urged dialogue to prevent further chaos. Economic activities have been severely disrupted, and Odinga's supporters are determined to fight for change through voting rather than violence, as many in his constituency face dire economic conditions.
